one_liner: Ahead-of-time compiler from a static JavaScript subset to WebAssembly; about 2.3x faster than V8 running the same numeric kernels.
what_it_does: jz compiles ordinary JavaScript modules (ES modules, arrow functions, classes, typed arrays, Map/Set, RegExp literals, JSON) to a standalone Wasm module, inferring types from the code rather than requiring annotations. Use it as `jz\`...\``/`jz(src, opts)` at run time, `compile()` plus `instantiate()` from `jz/interop` (a 13 KB gzipped marshalling runtime) for prebuilt modules, or the `jz kernel.js -O3` CLI; `--host wasi` emits a module for wasmtime and other standalone runtimes. It is not a drop-in engine: programs outside the subset (eval, Proxy, runtime prototype changes, DOM) are rejected or fall back to slower dynamic paths, and memory uses a bump allocator with no GC.
how_it_is_fast: Whole-program AOT analysis: type inference from literals, typed arrays and loop counters, fixed object layouts resolved at compile time, direct calls instead of dynamic dispatch, i32 narrowing of integer chains, and closure lowering, so the emitted Wasm has none of V8's type guards, hidden-class checks or GC barriers. Loops are vectorized to Wasm SIMD (v128) where possible, and from optimize level 2 float sum reductions are split into lanes (reassociated). Per-call arena rewinding replaces garbage collection.
when_to_use: Numeric typed-array kernels written in JavaScript (DSP filters, audio synthesis, image convolution and blur, small matrix math, hashing, parsers) where you want a 2-10x speedup without rewriting in Rust or C.
Shipping the same kernel to browsers and Node and to wasmtime or other WASI hosts from one JavaScript source (`--host wasi`).
Audio worklets and other real-time paths: `memory: { fixed: [...] }` proves at compile time that the named exports never allocate, grow memory or call the host.
Code you want to keep as plain JavaScript: removing the build step leaves source that still runs in any JS engine.
when_not_to_use: Dynamic JavaScript (eval, Proxy, Reflect, monkey-patching, prototype mutation, Intl, Temporal, DOM): rejected or left on slow dynamic paths.
Long-lived, allocation-heavy object graphs: there is no GC; what a call keeps lives until `memory.reset()`, replaced state is never freed and WeakMap/WeakRef hold strongly.

Code that needs exact JavaScript semantics: float sums may be reassociated (last digits differ), Math functions differ from V8 by up to 49 ulp, BigInt is 64-bit wrapping, compile-time constant chains use exact rationals, and bitwise operators on operands of 2^63 or more give -1 or 0.

Large real libraries: the bench's flagship whole-library case (web-audio-api, about 120 modules) runs 11.6x slower than V8 and fails its checksum in the committed results, and the self-compile rows (watr, jessie) lose to V8.
Production systems needing a stable ABI: pre-1.0, raw Wasm ABI not stable across versions, and the compiler changes many times a day (5,258 commits).

integration.form: npm module (`jz` 0.9.2, ESM) with CLI; output is a .wasm module plus the optional `jz/interop` runtime
integration.dependencies: subscript ^10.8.1 and watr ^5.11.9 (compiler only); the emitted module needs only `jz/interop` for value marshalling, or nothing for raw numeric exports
integration.min_toolchain: Node with ES modules (no `engines` field declared); the output uses Wasm SIMD and tail calls by default (`optimize: { simd: false, tailCall: false }` or `--no-simd`/`--no-tail-call` for engines without them)
integration.platforms: Any Wasm engine with SIMD and tail calls (V8 in Node and browsers, wasmtime via `--host wasi`); wasm32 only (4 GiB memory, 2^31-1 array elements)
integration.thread_safety: One instance is single-threaded; `memory: { shared: true }` compiles for threads and lowers Atomics to Wasm atomics, but strings, objects and Symbols stay local to their instance, and fixed-memory scratch storage belongs to one instance
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — the same .js source runs in V8 and compiles with jz, but only inside the supported subset, with the documented semantic differences, and callers go through `instantiate()`/exports instead of importing the module directly

gotchas: Harness flaw: in the committed bench/results.json, 54 of the 61 V8 rows carry no `measuredAt` provenance (carried from an earlier, unidentified run) while the jz rows were measured at e36aab3b; the partial-refresh anchor check re-measured only c-wasm on mat4 and fft and AssemblyScript on synth, never a V8 row, and the host recorded 25,065 MB swap and load average 7.92.

The V8 baseline is the slowest JS JIT in the table (Deno, also V8, is close): Node v25.9.0 takes 1.22x the time of Bun and 1.25x that of JavaScriptCore by geomean over 57 cases, and more than 1.5x on 13-16 of them (mat4 8,498 vs 2,495 us on Bun; dispatch 8,797 vs 2,363 us), so jz's geomean ratio is 0.55 against Bun and 0.56 against JSC rather than 0.44 against V8 (derived from page data). Cases whose checksum fails drop out of every geomean, including webaudio, where jz is 11.6x slower than V8.

Some of the biggest wins rely on float reassociation ('Float sums in lanes' from optimize level 2) that neither V8 nor the strict clang reference (-ffp-contract=off, no -ffast-math) may do: dotprod runs 148 us under jz vs 891 us native C vs 2,055 us V8, and its inputs are integer-valued so the reassociated sum cannot change the checksum. checksumF64 hashes only the low 32-bit word of every 128th f64 (for mat4, only out[0]), so parity checks are sparse.

The README's cross-language claim (C, Rust and Zig compiled to Wasm about 2x behind jz) compares SIMD-less builds: bench.mjs builds c-wasm, rust-wasm and zig-wasm with no simd128 target feature while jz emits v128 by default. The bench README prose is also stale against results.json: it says native clang leads by 1.2x and V8 wins the deopt probes, but the committed data gives jz/native 0.96 over 50 cases and jz ahead of V8 on dispatch, shapes, wordcount, immutable and strbuild.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Its siblings are Wasm engines (Wasmtime, WAMR, wasm3, Wasmi) and compilers from other source languages (wasm2c, AssemblyScript is its own baseline); pick jz when the source is JavaScript and you want it compiled to Wasm rather than run in a JIT or in an interpreter shipped inside Wasm (Javy, ComponentizeJS with weval). For C, C++ or Rust sources, compile them with their own toolchains and SIMD enabled.
verified_claims_summary: On an Apple M4 Max (Node v25.9.0, clang 19.1.6, asc 0.28.19, jz 0.9.2), the project's own harness (5 warm-up runs, median of 21) gives jz-compiled Wasm on V8 a geometric-mean time ratio of 0.425 versus the same JS on V8 over 53 non-lab cases with matching checksums (faster on 52) and 0.448 versus AssemblyScript -O3 over 50 cases; jz under wasmtime is 0.498 of V8 over 52 cases. The kernels are author-chosen numeric workloads, most V8 rows are from an older unidentified run, and the dataset is flagged partial.
status_note: Very active (commits daily up to 2026-10-06, 174 stars, 1 open issue) and MIT-licensed, but pre-1.0 and experimental with an unstable Wasm ABI; usable today for self-contained numeric kernels if you pin the version and re-test on upgrade.
